title: Pakistan Electricity Bill Index (Monthly) | Wattlyst
meta: Monthly bill for 100, 200, 300 and 500 units in LESCO, IESCO, K-Electric and every DISCO, with the change from last month, method and a free CSV download.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: How the bill changed from September 2026 to October 2026
p: The base tariff (energy rates and fixed charges) has not changed since NEPRA's February notification, so the monthly movement comes from the add-ons. The fuel price adjustment (FPA) charged in October 2026 bills is Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, against Rs 2.52 per unit for July 2026 in September 2026 bills. The quarterly adjustment for 2026-09 to 2026-11 is the same in both months.

For an unprotected home the FPA is charged on every unit and GST is added on top, so a 300 unit bill is down Rs 498 (3.4%) and a 500 unit bill is down Rs 830 (3%). Protected homes are exempt from the FPA, so their bills did not move.

sections.h2: Is the bill the same in LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO and K-Electric?
p: Yes for the base tariff: since the tariff rationalisation notified in February, A-1 domestic energy rates and fixed charges are uniform across the ten ex-WAPDA distribution companies and K-Electric, and the August fuel adjustment was notified for all of them. That is why every company in the table above shows the same bill for the same units.

Real bills can still differ by a few rupees: billing days, the meter reading date, arrears, the TV fee where it is still charged, and any company-specific adjustment. Use your company's bill calculator with your own units and sanctioned load for an exact estimate.

Each bill = energy charge (protected: slab by slab with the benefit of one previous slab; unprotected: all units at the rate of the slab reached) + fixed charge for a 2 kW sanctioned load + FC surcharge + quarterly adjustment + fuel price adjustment (not for protected consumers) + GST on the subtotal. Rates come from the NEPRA tariff file Wattlyst keeps with its source and checked date; the monthly FPA comes from the NEPRA decision or, until it is published on nepra.org.pk, a dated news report of the notification (marked in the CSV).

The index is rebuilt every month: the new month is added at the top and earlier months are kept, so the CSV is a running history. Corrections go to the contact page; a corrected figure is noted on this page.

Wattlyst's Pakistan Electricity Bill Index for October 2026: a household using 300 units pays about Rs 14,264 (down Rs 498 (3.4%) from September 2026); 200 units cost Rs 8,678 unprotected and Rs 4,372 protected; 500 units cost Rs 27,028. The fuel adjustment in October 2026 bills is Rs 1.11 per unit. Source: Wattlyst Pakistan Electricity Bill Index, computed from NEPRA tariff data; free to quote with a link.

faq.q: What is the electricity bill for 300 units in October 2026?
faq.a: About Rs 14,264 for an unprotected home with a 2 kW connection, including the fixed charge, surcharges, FPA and GST. That is Rs 47.55 per unit all-in.

faq.q: What is the bill for 200 units for a protected consumer?
faq.a: About Rs 4,372 in October 2026 bills. Protected consumers pay lower slab rates and no fuel price adjustment; an unprotected home using the same units pays Rs 8,678.

faq.q: Why did my bill change this month if the tariff did not?
faq.a: Mostly because of the monthly fuel price adjustment: Rs 1.11 per unit in October 2026 bills against Rs 2.52 the month before. More units in a hotter month, a longer billing cycle or crossing a slab line also change the bill.

faq.q: Is K-Electric cheaper than LESCO or IESCO?
faq.a: Not for the base tariff: the A-1 domestic rates and fixed charges are uniform across K-Electric and the ex-WAPDA companies, so the same units give the same bill in this index. Small differences on real bills come from billing days and company-specific items.

faq.q: Can I use this data in an article or report?
faq.a: Yes. The index is free to reuse under CC BY 4.0: credit Wattlyst and link to this page. The CSV download has every line of every bill.

faq.q: How often is the index updated?
faq.a: Every month, after NEPRA notifies the fuel price adjustment for the month two months earlier. The last checked date is shown under Sources.

key_facts: October 2026: 100 units cost an unprotected home Rs 3,870 and a protected home Rs 2,158; 200 units cost Rs 8,678 unprotected and Rs 4,372 protected.
300 units cost Rs 14,264 (Rs 47.55 per unit all-in) and 500 units cost Rs 27,028 (Rs 54.06 per unit) in October 2026 bills.
The fuel price adjustment in October 2026 bills is Rs 1.11 per unit for the fuel used in August 2026; protected consumers do not pay it, so their bills are unchanged from September 2026.
Every figure is computed by the Wattlyst bill engine from the NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff, for a 2 kW sanctioned load, and can be reproduced with the bill calculator.
The index is published monthly and is free to reuse with a link (CC BY 4.0); the CSV download carries every line of every bill.

sources.label: NEPRA tariff decision and SRO 279(I)/2026 for A-1 domestic consumers (tariff PDF)
October 2026 bills: Express Tribune, 8 October 2026: NEPRA notifies Rs 1.11 per unit fuel adjustment for August in October bills (ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric)
September 2026 bills: NEPRA decision on the fuel charges adjustment for July 2026, ex-WAPDA DISCOs, SRO 1499(I)/2026
